P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Icelandic banks offer unrestricted foreign-currency accounts (gjaldeyrisreikningur óbundinn): Arion banki publishes a consumer payment-account fee schedule for one, dated 7 May 2026, covering deposits into and withdrawals from the account in krónur or foreign notes (Arion banki). The capital controls imposed in 2008 were largely lifted in 2017 (see P1).

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A sole proprietorship (einstaklingsfyrirtæki) is recorded in the Business Register at Skatturinn (Directorate of Internal Revenue). You first need an Icelandic ID number (kennitala) from the National Registry (Þjóðskrá). Then register with Skatturinn for income tax, and for VAT once turnover passes ISK 2,000,000 in 12 months (see L4). Registration can usually be completed online through the government portal. With no business name (trading under your own name) there is usually no registration fee. EEA/EFTA nationals can register without special authorisation; others need residence and work permits first. No minimum capital; unlimited personal liability.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Official TIN description supplied by Iceland to the OECD: "The Icelandic Identification Number (kennitala) is used as a TIN in Iceland. This number is a unique number issued to both individuals and entities. The TIN has a special structure depending on the type of taxpayer. Register Iceland issues the identification number for individuals and Fyrirtækjaskrá issues the identification number for entities. TINs are used for all taxes in Iceland." L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Progressive national plus municipal tax (rates not captured). Residents are generally taxed on worldwide income (see quoted rules). Work performed while living in Iceland for foreign clients is generally taxable there. 2026 income tax brackets (monthly income, incl. municipal tax): 31.49% up to ISK 498,122, 37.99% up to ISK 1,398,450, and 46.29% above. Self-employed people must also pay themselves a deemed salary (reiknað endurgjald) at no less than the Director of Internal Revenue's reference amounts for their sector (2026 amounts not captured).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 24% standard and 11% reduced, with exports zero-rated. Self-employed business owners selling taxable goods and services must register for VAT. They are exempt from registering if sales are ISK 2,000,000 or less in each twelve-month period from the start of their activity (raised from ISK 1,000,000 in 2017). Foreign taxable persons follow the same rules; foreign e-service suppliers to Icelandic consumers can use the simplified VOES scheme.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The GDPR applies in Iceland through the EEA Agreement (incorporated by the EEA Joint Committee in July 2018). Act No. 90/2018 on Data Protection implements the GDPR; supervisor: Persónuvernd.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
